request: How large is the immigration court backlog and how has it changed over time?

reply.reply:
**At the end of FY2024, the immigration-court backlog was 3,558,995 pending cases; an earlier report put it at approximately 1.6 million in December 2021, and CRS says pending cases increased every year since FY2006.**

- At the end of FY2024, the immigration courts had 3,558,995 pending cases. (IN12492, PDF p. 4)
- The report states that pending cases increased every year since FY2006. (R47077, PDF p. 21)
- In the first quarter of FY2022, pending cases exceeded 1.5 million; TRAC estimated approximately 1.6 million in December 2021. (R47077, PDF p. 21)
- Immigration court caseloads generally increased since 1983, and annual receipts rose more significantly after FY2019 except during FY2020 and FY2021. (IN12492, PDF p. 2)
reply.reasoning: CRS’s FY2024 figure indicates the scale of the backlog; an earlier CRS report provides a December 2021 comparison and says pending cases had increased each year since FY2006. The figures refer to different dates and should be treated as snapshots.
